title: Camera bore ground-track speed derivation
note: OneNote .one format; derivation reconstructed from canonical source code (image_quality.py, camera_optics.py, camera_image.py, SATELLITE.py).

handwriting: Camera bore ground speed derivation — referenced from image_quality.py::analytic_bore_ground_velocity_disk_m_s
Boresight unit: d_hat = [cos(phi), sin(phi)], phi_dot = omega_body
Ray-ellipsoid: A t^2 + B t + C = 0, t* = positive root
t_dot = -(A_dot * t*^2 + B_dot * t* + C_dot) / (2 A t* + B)
g_dot = s_dot + t_dot * d_hat + t* * d_dot
figure_annotations: Sketch of orbit disk with satellite position, boresight ray, and WGS84 ellipse intersection.
Annotations show orbit velocity vector, body rotation omega_body, and ground hit displacement during exposure.

summary: The camera bore ground-track speed is computed analytically via implicit differentiation of the ray-ellipsoid intersection (WGS84) with respect to time. Inputs: satellite orbital angle + rate, body angle + rate, boresight direction. Output: v_bore [m/s] -> ground blur delta = v_bore * t_exp [m] -> quality q = r/(delta+r), r=0.30m, t_exp=100us. Nadir at 540 km gives q~0.28; perfect target tracking gives q~1.0.
